Scale and detail

Detail level should match the gift. A mini hoop with two clear symbols can be completed quickly; a full workshop or office scene takes far longer and may lose the appeal of a simple gift.

Work in stitch dimensions rather than pixels alone. The same artwork may work at 120 stitches wide and lose its identity completely when reduced to 45. Color and style

Adding a name, job title or short phrase can increase value, but avoid filling the piece with text. The main visual object should remain readable at first glance.

Limit colors deliberately. Every extra shade should add volume, separation or identity; if it appears in only a few stitches without changing the image, it may add work rather than quality. Composition and personalization

For technical professions, basic object accuracy matters. An incorrect formula or impossible instrument can be especially obvious to the person who actually works in the field.

Think about the final use as well: gift, framed art, mini, collection or personalization. Rights and accuracy where relevant

Avoid copying specific uniforms, badges, logos or brands when they are unnecessary. Generic original visual language is better for a reusable commercial collection.
